prompts.text: Name a female singer with over 500,000 monthly listeners on Spotify

items.quip: Cape Verde's barefoot diva performed morna onstage without shoes.
items.title: Cesária Évora
items.extract: Cesária Évora GCIH was a Cape Verdean singer known for singing morna, a genre of music from Cape Verde, in her native Cape Verdean Creole. Her songs were often devoted to themes of love, homesickness, nostalgia, and the history of the Cape Verdean people. She was known for performing barefoot and for her habit of smoking and drinking on stage during intermissions. Évora's music received many accolades, including a Grammy Award in 2004, and it has influenced many Cape Verde diaspora musicians as well as American pop singer Madonna. Évora is also known as Cize, the Barefoot Diva, and the Queen of Morna.

items.quip: Argentina's junta banned her, and she sang on from exile.
items.title: Mercedes Sosa
items.extract: Haydée Marta Mercedes Sosa Girón was an Argentine singer who was popular throughout Latin America and many countries outside the region. With her roots in Argentine folk music, Sosa became one of the preeminent exponents of the nuevo cancionero movement. She gave voice to songs written by many Latin American songwriters. She was hailed as the "voice of the voiceless ones", and often called "the conscience of Latin America".

items.quip: Harvard's 1892 football play is still outlawed in rugby's laws.
items.title: Flying wedge
items.extract: A flying wedge is a configuration created from a body moving forward in a triangular formation. This V-shaped arrangement began as a successful military strategy in ancient times when infantry units would move forward in wedge formations to smash through an enemy's lines. This principle was later used by Medieval European armies, as well as modern armed forces, which have adapted the V-shaped wedge for armored assault.

items.quip: NFL referees may award a touchdown to punish one.
items.title: Unfair act
items.extract: In American football, an unfair act is a foul that can be called when a player or team commits a flagrant and obviously illegal act that has a major impact on the game, and from which, if additional penalties were not enforced, the offending team would gain an advantage.

prompts.text: Name a university in the US or UK

items.quip: Kentucky college that has charged no tuition since 1892.
items.title: Berea College
items.description: Work college in Berea, Kentucky, US
items.extract: Berea College is a private liberal arts work college in Berea, Kentucky, United States. Founded in 1855, it was the first college in the Southern United States to be coeducational and racially integrated. It admitted non-White students from as early as 1866 until 1904, and again after 1954.

items.quip: All graduates study one dual degree: naval architecture and marine engineering.
items.title: Webb Institute
items.extract: Webb Institute is a private college specialized in engineering and located in Glen Cove, New York, United States. Each graduate of Webb Institute earns a Bachelor of Science degree in naval architecture and marine engineering. The school is noted in the marine industry for its emphasis on ship design and systems engineering, its practical work experience, and its free tuition for domestic students.

prompts.text: Name a fruit normally eaten with its skin on

items.quip: Its miraculin makes sour foods like lemons taste sweet.
items.title: Synsepalum dulcificum
items.description: Plant from West Africa with a taste-modifying berry
items.extract: Synsepalum dulcificum is a plant in the Sapotaceae family, native to tropical Africa. It is known for its berry that, when eaten, causes sour foods subsequently consumed to taste sweet. Common names for this species and its berry include miracle fruit, miracle berry, miraculous berry, sweet berry, and in West Africa, where the species originates, àgbáyun, taami, asaa, and ledidi.
